sources.actual_access: Original PDF text parsed by web tool, original downloaded via curl; printed57 rendered locally and visually inspected. Web screenshot attempt failed Cache miss before local success.
accepted_claims: A qualitative study of tools in selected Odisha and West Bengal villages identifies kula as a winnower.
Table55 lists kula, bamboo sieve and jhuri separately; Odisha columns are Mobarakpur and Baredeswar.
limits: Not a current statewide prevalence survey or craft-making manual.
Does not explicitly assign bamboo material to kula; use NIE for that material claim.
Narrative universal-tool claim conflicts with several table percentages. Exclude generalized every-household statements; no percentages needed.
Related 2015 Sarkar et al. research article listed in report is the same research family, not independently inspected.
sources.rights: No image-reuse licence established; captured page retained internally for review only. No report image proposed for public article.

sources.title: Agricultural engineering in development: Post-harvest operations and management of foodgrains
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.locator: Grain cleaning and insecticide treatments: Cleaning; Traditional methods; Winnowers. Web extraction lines13–46. Contents/title page lines0–19 confirms authors, series and copyright1994.
sources.actual_access: Both original FAO pages opened and read through web tool. Separate urllib capture attempt returned403; no locally downloaded original HTML claimed.
accepted_claims: Winnowing tosses grain into air so wind removes lighter impurities.
That operation does not remove heavier impurities such as gravel.
The machine description distinguishes air separation from sieves sorting by size; this is general explanation, not an Odisha field observation.
limits: No evidence here for local makers, dates, tray construction or a universal regional gesture.
Do not imply a traditional kula contains a machine fan or sieves.
Exclude insecticides and treatment guidance; no claim of complete food safety or grain cleanliness.
sources.rights: Title page says all rights reserved. Paraphrase and link; no illustration adopted.

accepted_claims: In the2018 report, Gurumurthy and Sridevi of Maderi Street, Malkangiri, made bamboo kula, pachiya and binchana for local markets.
The reporter distinguishes a winnowing fan, wicker basket and hand fan.
The report records makers describing weaker demand, material-cost and market-linkage pressures in2018; attribute as dated testimony, not present conditions.
limits: Opening dyed-strip weaving sequence belongs to P Daligurulu's dala basket, not to a kula; never transfer it into a kula recipe.
Exclude counts, income, prices, age/origin and promises of assistance as unnecessary or unverified current claims.
Do not identify the Commons photograph as these makers' work or as Malkangiri.
Earlier2017 NIE source already reused in Binchana; publisher/reporting family kept together conservatively if both enter new prose.
